Africa holds 60% of the world’s best solar potential, a $190B clean energy opportunity.
 
At yesterday’s fireside chat on #Africa’s energy future, I argued that innovation here must mean access and industrialization first—not just decarbonization. Momentum is real, but what’s missing is bold finance, regional integration, and political will to make Africa not just a consumer, but a clean energy engine.
 
The paradox is clear: with 60% of solar potential and 30% of critical minerals, Africa still has 600M people without electricity—85% of the global deficit—while receiving just 2% of clean energy investment. Without action, we risk a green-tech divide.
 
Countries in Africa are closing the gap by: 
1️⃣ Deploying decentralized innovation at scale – as is already happening in Kenya’s EcoSafi stoves which halve cooking costs; and Nigeria’s containerized mini-grids which  power villages in a day. Together, such models could reach 380M people by 2030 at the lowest cost.
2️⃣ Leveraging #digital and #AI breakthroughs – from UNDP & IBM ’s geospatial forecasting tool to M-KOPA’s AI-driven financing, digital innovation is the backbone of Africa’s industrial revolution.
3️⃣ Turning mineral wealth into local prosperity – instead of exporting bauxite at $65/ton and importing aluminum at $2,335/ton, Africa must process locally. With copper, cobalt, nickel, and lithium worth $16T over 25 years, Sub-Saharan Africa could capture $2T by building domestic industries.
 
The opportunity is historic: with $190B/year in clean energy investment by 2030, Africa can close its access gap, fuel industrialization, and drive global energy innovation.
